titulo: Future Forms: will / going to / present continuous
descripcion: At A2 you use going to for plans and will for quick decisions and predictions. The present continuous for fixed arrangements comes more fully at B1. This is the first step towards more precise time reference at higher levels.

filas: I'll help you. / It will rain.

ejemplos.texto: I'm going to study tonight after dinner.
I'm meeting her at six tomorrow.

notas: Going to is for something already decided or planned.
Will is for a decision made at the moment of speaking.
The present continuous can express the future with a time word, for arrangements.

contraste.es: Spanish uses voy a very much like going to, so the structure transfers directly.
contraste.de: German often uses the present for the future (Morgen besuche ich meine Oma), which leads to Tomorrow I visit my grandma instead of I'm going to visit. Be careful with will: ich will means I want, not I will.
contraste.it: Italian often uses the present for the future (domani parto), which leads to Tomorrow I leave instead of I'm going to leave or I'm leaving. The Italian future corresponds to will for predictions.
contraste.fr: French je vais + infinitive corresponds exactly to going to (je vais visiter ma grand-mère – I'm going to visit my grandma), and the French future to will. French speakers therefore transfer the two forms well.
contraste.pt: Portuguese vou + infinitive (vou visitar a minha avó) corresponds exactly to going to, so plans transfer directly. The simple future is rare in spoken Portuguese, so Portuguese speakers tend to under-use will.

errores: Using will for something already planned.
Using going to for a spontaneous decision.

traducciones.de: Ich werde… / Ich habe vor, … zu…

redemittel.expresion: What are you going to do?

autochequeo: Is going to used for a plan?
Is will used for a spontaneous decision?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on going to versus will. Check whether each matches how planned the event is. Do not rewrite the text. Flag any confusion between the two. Flag anything unclear.

es: *te llamo mañana* rendered in the present: *I call you tomorrow* instead of *I'll call you tomorrow*.
de: Inverting after a time word, as German V2 does: *Tomorrow go I to Bern* instead of *Tomorrow I'm going to Bern*.
it: *ti chiamo domani* rendered in the present: *I call you tomorrow* instead of *I'll call you tomorrow*.
fr: *je t'appelle demain* rendered in the present: *I call you tomorrow* instead of *I'll call you tomorrow*.
pt: *ligo-te amanhã* rendered in the present: *I call you tomorrow* instead of *I'll call you tomorrow*.
